critical_failures: Misstates the extension policy by claiming a 2026-02-11 hold exceeds the two-day limit, when it falls within it.
Would wrongly refuse a policy-compliant request and push the customer toward an earlier date without any visible basis.
judgment.explanation: The proposal misreads the visible policy. event-001 says DL-007 is held until 2026-02-09 18:00 UTC. It allows a single two-day extension if requested before expiry and if capacity permits, and it says capacity currently exists. Ciro's request in event-002 was made on 2026-02-08, before expiry. He asks to hold the item until 2026-02-11, which is two days past 2026-02-09, so it fits the policy. The proposed message says the date "exceeds the two-day extension policy" and asks him to pick an earlier date. That contradicts the visible evidence and would wrongly turn down a policy-compliant request. A better next contact would confirm or route the extension to 2026-02-11, after any needed staff approval, or ask a real clarifying question such as whether the hold ends at 18:00 UTC on that day. The message also gives no alternatives or dates, so "choose an earlier date" is not an actionable choice. The recipient and channel are correct, because Ciro wrote through the customer portal. The message is unsent and makes no unauthorized commitment, but it states the policy wrongly and does not address the actual request.
